# keychain.nvim

Keep secrets out of your `.env` files. `keychain.nvim` stores real values in the
**macOS Keychain** and leaves only safe references in `.env`, plus a
diagnostics pass that flags plaintext-looking secrets you (or a teammate)
accidentally typed in.

```
# .env (safe to commit)
DEBUG=true
API_KEY=keychain://API_KEY
DATABASE_PASSWORD=keychain://DATABASE_PASSWORD
```

```
# .env.local (generated, gitignored - what your app actually reads)
# Generated by keychain.nvim - do not edit, run :KeychainSync to regenerate
DEBUG=true
API_KEY=sk_live_...
DATABASE_PASSWORD=hunter2...
```

## Requirements

- Neovim >= 0.10
- macOS (uses the built-in `security` CLI to talk to the login Keychain)

## Installation

**lazy.nvim**

```lua
{
  "yourname/keychain.nvim",
  cmd = {
    "KeychainSet",
    "KeychainGet",
    "KeychainDelete",
    "KeychainMigrate",
    "KeychainSync",
    "KeychainLoad",
    "KeychainUnload",
  },
  opts = {},
}
```

**packer.nvim**

```lua
use({
  "yourname/keychain.nvim",
  config = function()
    require("keychain").setup()
  end,
})
```

`keychain.nvim` never calls `setup()` for you; you must call
`require("keychain").setup({...})` (or pass `opts = {}` with lazy.nvim) from
your config.

## How it works

- Each project gets its own Keychain "service" (`nvim-env:<git-root-or-cwd>`),
  so the same key name in two different projects never collides.
- `.env` files only ever contain `KEY=keychain://ACCOUNT` references. The
  actual secret lives solely in the macOS Keychain.
- `:KeychainSync` resolves those references into a real, plaintext file
  (default `.env.local`) for tools/processes that need actual environment
  variables at runtime, and offers to add it to `.gitignore` automatically.
- `:KeychainLoad` is an alternative to `:KeychainSync` for apps you run from
  inside Neovim (e.g. via `:terminal` or `jobstart()`): it resolves the same
  references but sets them on `vim.env` instead of writing a file, so
  nothing touches disk. Because environment variables are only inherited by
  a process at the moment it's spawned, this only reaches processes started
  *after* `:KeychainLoad` runs and *as children of Neovim* - an
  already-open `:terminal`, or an app started outside Neovim entirely,
  won't see the update. Run `:KeychainUnload` to clear what was loaded.
- A background diagnostics scanner flags lines that look like plaintext
  secrets (based on key name + value entropy/length) with `vim.diagnostic`
  warnings. It never blocks saving - it's advisory only.

## Commands

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `:KeychainSet [KEY]` | Prompt (masked input) for a secret value, store it in the Keychain, and write/replace `KEY=keychain://KEY` at the cursor (or append it). Without `KEY`, uses the key on the current line or prompts for one. |
| `:KeychainGet [KEY]` | Look up the secret for `KEY` (or the ref/key under the cursor), show it briefly in a floating window, and yank it to a scratch register (`@z` by default). Both auto-clear after `reveal_seconds`. |
| `:KeychainMigrate` | Scan the current buffer for plaintext-looking secrets and interactively move each one into the Keychain, replacing it with a reference. |
| `:KeychainSync [target]` | Resolve every `keychain://` reference in the current `.env` into a real file (default `.env.local`), and offer to add it to `.gitignore`. |
| `:KeychainLoad` | Resolve every `keychain://` reference (and plain value) in the current `.env` buffer and set them directly on `vim.env` for this Neovim session - no file is written. Only processes started from Neovim *after* this runs (`:terminal`, `jobstart()`, etc.) will inherit them. |
| `:KeychainUnload` | Unset every env var previously set by `:KeychainLoad` in this session. |
| `:KeychainDelete [KEY]` | Delete a Keychain entry (with confirmation). |

## Configuration

Defaults (pass any subset to `setup()` to override):

```lua
require("keychain").setup({
  service_prefix = "nvim-env:",
  project_id_strategy = "git_root", -- or "cwd"

  env_file_patterns = { "^%.env$", "^%.env%.[%w_.-]+$" },
  env_file_ignore_patterns = { "%.example$", "%.sample$", "%.template$" },

  sync = {
    target = ".env.local",
    add_marker = true,
    auto_gitignore = true,
  },

  detection = {
    enabled = true,
    min_entropy = 3.0,
    min_length = 8,
    min_entropy_unnamed = 3.6,
    min_length_unnamed = 20,
    key_patterns = { "SECRET", "TOKEN", "PASSWORD", "API[_-]?KEY", "..." },
    ignore_values = { "^changeme$", "^xxx+$", "..." },
  },

  reveal_seconds = 10,
  scratch_register = "z",
})
```

## Security notes / caveats

- Secrets are passed to the `security` CLI as argv values (never
  shell-interpolated), but they will still appear in `argv` for the lifetime
  of that short-lived process, which is visible to other processes owned by
  the same user (e.g. via `ps`). This is an inherent limitation of shelling
  out to `security` from any tool, not specific to this plugin.
  `:KeychainGet` uses a dedicated scratch register rather than the system
  clipboard to reduce exposure to clipboard managers/history.
- `:KeychainSync` writes real secrets to disk in plaintext (that's the point
  - some tools need a real `.env`). Make sure the target is gitignored (the
    plugin offers to do this for you) and treat it like any other secret
  file.
- `:KeychainLoad` avoids writing to disk, but secrets still end up in
  Neovim's process environment for the rest of the session (until
  `:KeychainUnload` or quitting Neovim), which remains visible to other
  processes owned by the same user (e.g. `ps eww <pid>`) - the same class of
  exposure noted above for the `security` CLI itself.
- The plaintext-secret diagnostics are heuristic (key-name patterns +
  entropy/length) and will have false positives/negatives. It's a nudge, not
  a guarantee - review with `:KeychainMigrate` rather than relying on it
  blindly.

## Testing

Tests use [plenary.nvim](https://github.com/nvim-lua/plenary.nvim)'s test
harness:

```sh
PLENARY_PATH=~/.local/share/nvim/lazy/plenary.nvim \
  nvim --headless -u tests/minimal_init.lua \
  -c "PlenaryBustedDirectory tests/keychain/ { minimal_init = 'tests/minimal_init.lua' }"
```

(`PLENARY_PATH` defaults to the common lazy.nvim install location if you
don't set it.)
